t.6.21.1: Then the spies reported to the lord of Laṅkā that Rāghava, whose might was unshakable, had encamped on Mount Suvela.
t.6.21.2: Rāvaṇa, having heard from his spies that the mighty Rāma had arrived, grew somewhat alarmed and spoke these words to Śārdūla.
t.6.21.4: Thus addressed by him, Śārdūla, overwhelmed with fear, then softly spoke these words to that tiger among rākṣasas.
t.6.21.3: Your complexion is not as it should be, and you look dejected, O night-wanderer. I hope you have not fallen into the power of angry enemies?
t.6.21.5: O king, those bulls among monkeys cannot be spied upon, for they are valiant and mighty, and they are protected by Rāghava.
t.6.21.6: They cannot even be spoken to, and no questioning is possible here. The path is guarded on every side by monkeys like mountains.
t.6.21.7: The very moment I entered that impenetrable army, I was recognized; seized by force by many, I was mauled in many ways.
t.6.21.8: Struck violently with knees, fists, teeth and palms, I have been led about by the mighty, wrathful monkeys.
t.6.21.9: And after being led around everywhere, I was brought to Rāma's assembly, my whole body smeared with blood, distraught, my senses reeling.
t.6.21.10: While I was being struck down by the monkeys, I begged for mercy with joined palms; rescued by Rāghava, I live, indeed, only by chance.
t.6.21.11: Having filled the great ocean with mountains and rocks, this Rāma, armed with his weapons, stands having taken his position at the gate of Laṅkā.
t.6.21.12: Having released me, that one of great splendor, surrounded on all sides by monkeys and arrayed in the Garuḍa formation, is advancing straight on Laṅkā.
t.6.21.13: Before he reaches the rampart, quickly do one of the two: either give Sītā to him at once, or let a good battle be offered.
t.6.21.14: Having heard that weighty speech of Śārdūla, the lord of the rākṣasas was tormented in his mind; then that Rāvaṇa spoke.
t.6.21.15: Even if the Devas, Gandharvas and Dānavas were to fight against me, I would never give up Sītā, not even out of fear of all the worlds.
t.6.21.16: Having spoken thus, the greatly splendid Rāvaṇa spoke again: "The army has been reconnoitred by you; which of the monkeys here are the heroes?"
t.6.21.17: What are they like, and of what might, these vānaras who are so hard to assail? Whose sons and whose grandsons are they? Tell me that, O Rākṣasa.
t.6.21.18: Having learned their strength and weakness, I shall then decide what is to be done in this matter. One who desires battle must certainly make a reckoning of the forces.
t.6.21.19: Then Śārdūla, the foremost of spies, thus addressed by Rāvaṇa, began to speak these words in Rāvaṇa's presence.
t.6.21.20: Then, O king, there is the son of Ṛkṣarajas, exceedingly hard to conquer in battle; and here is the son of Gadgada, renowned by the name Jāmbavān.
t.6.21.22: And here too, O king, is the righteous and valiant Suṣeṇa, son of Dharma, and the gentle monkey Dadhimukha, son of Soma.
t.6.21.21: Here is another son of Gadgada, the son of Śatakratu's preceptor, whose son alone wrought a great slaughter of the Rākṣasas.
t.6.21.23: Here too are Sumukha and Durmukha, and the monkey Vegadarśī; surely Death itself has been created by Svayambhū in the form of a monkey.
t.6.21.24: And there is Nīla, the son of the fire-god, himself the commander of the army; and here is the son of the wind-god, renowned as Hanūmān.
t.6.21.25: The grandson of Śakra, the young and mighty Aṅgada, is hard to overcome; and Mainda and Dvivida, both powerful, were born of the Aśvins.
t.6.21.26: Here are the five sons of Vaivasvata, each like Kāla the Destroyer: Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Śarabha and Gandhamādana.
t.6.21.27: Here are Śveta and Jyotirmukha, the two sons born of Bhāskara, and there too is Hemakūṭa, the monkey, son of Varuṇa.
t.6.21.29: There are ten crores of monkeys besides, heroes eager for battle, glorious sons of the gods; the rest of them I cannot bring myself to enumerate.
t.6.21.28: Here is the heroic Nala, son of Viśvakarman, best of monkeys, valiant and swift; and here too is the son of a Vasu, exceedingly hard to withstand.
t.6.21.30: This is the son of Daśaratha, a youth with the build of a lion, by whom Dūṣaṇa was slain, and Khara and Triśiras as well.
t.6.21.31: There is no one on earth equal to Rāma in valour, by whom Virādha was slain, and Kabandha too, who was like Antaka himself.
t.6.21.32: No man on earth is able to tell the virtues of Rāma, by whom so many rākṣasas who had gone to Janasthāna were slain.
t.6.21.33: And here is Lakṣmaṇa, righteous of soul, like a bull among elephants; having come within the path of his arrows, not even Vāsava would survive.
t.6.21.34: And your brother Vibhīṣaṇa, the foremost of the Rākṣasas, having taken possession of the city of Laṅkā, is devoted to the welfare of Rāghava.
t.6.21.35: Thus this entire monkey army, stationed on Mount Suvela, has been fully described to you; in what remains to be done, you are the refuge.
